extrapolatedBulkEstimate.note: Extrapolation conservative: 30% canary rate. Failure modes seen — paywall outlets with stale or missing cookies (WSJ 401, WashPost paywall+404, Bloomberg bot-block); 404'd URLs (Vulture article slug rotated); bot-blocked outlets (TalkinBroadway 403); multi-show roundup index pages that fail garbage gate (gotham-playgoer). Refreshing paywall cookies (WSJ/WaPo/Bloomberg) before Phase B could lift rate to 45-55%.

reasoning: 30% canary success — exactly the threshold the spec called out for reconsideration. Bulk run would recover ~300 of 1009 files at this rate.

Cohort dropped from 1582 to 1009 after filtering: 364 no-url, 166 fabricatedEntry, 43 gating flags. The 1551/1400-1600 figure in the spec was an estimate; actual targets are 1009 (still a meaningful catalog cleanup).
Successful pathways: ScrapingBee (NYT paywalled w/ cookies), Browserbase (THR), Archive.org (theater.nytimes.com legacy URL). All three tiers are working.
Failure pathways indicate fixable infrastructure gaps:
- 3/7 fails are paywall outlets where cookies look fresh on disk but get 401/paywall blocks (cookies expired).
- 2/7 fails are URL rot (Vulture 404, TalkinBroadway 403) — partial mitigation via Wayback fallback (worked for Pre-2011).
- 1/7 fails is correct rejection of a multi-show index page (Blog) — accept this as data quality.
- 1/7 fails is SERP fallback couldn't find URL (Bloomberg) — could try archive.today / Wayback first instead.

BEFORE Phase B: refresh WSJ/WaPo/Bloomberg cookies, then re-canary 5 of those domains. If rate >= 50% on re-canary, PROCEED. If still ~30%, accept the 300 yield (Phase B cost is <$30, very low ROI threshold to clear).
If proceeding now without cookie refresh: PROCEED at risk — total upside is small (~300 cleaned llmScores) but cost is also small. Phase B is a reasonable cleanup operation either way.
